title: Duties of a Citizen
subtitle: Responsibilities, defending Canada, equality, and who we are

questions.question: What are three responsibilities of citizenship?
options: Being loyal to Canada, recycling newspapers, serving in the navy, army or air force
Obeying the law, taking responsibility for oneself and one's family, serving on a jury
Learning both official languages, voting in elections, belonging to a union
Buying Canadian products, owning your own business, using less water
questions.explanation: This is one of the sample questions printed in the guide. Responsibilities include obeying the law, taking responsibility for oneself and one's family, serving on a jury, voting in elections, helping others in the community, and protecting our heritage and environment.

questions.question: Which principle means that no person or group is above the law and that governments are regulated by laws, not arbitrary actions?
questions.explanation: One of Canada's founding principles is the rule of law. Individuals and governments are regulated by laws and not by arbitrary actions, and no person or group is above the law.

questions.question: When you are called to serve on a jury, what are you required to do?
options: You may decline if you are busy
You are legally required to serve
You must pay a fee to be excused
You only serve if you are a lawyer
questions.explanation: When called to do so, you are legally required to serve on a jury. Serving on a jury is a privilege that makes the justice system work, because it depends on impartial juries made up of citizens.

questions.question: What are some examples of taking responsibility for yourself and your family?
options: Getting a job, taking care of one's family and working hard in keeping with one's abilities
Joining a political party and voting
questions.explanation: Getting a job, taking care of one's family and working hard in keeping with one's abilities are important Canadian values. Work contributes to personal dignity and self-respect, and to Canada's prosperity.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of helping others in the community, as described in the guide?
options: Volunteering at a food bank or encouraging newcomers to integrate
questions.explanation: Millions of volunteers donate their time to help others without pay: helping people in need, assisting at a child's school, volunteering at a food bank or charity, or encouraging newcomers to integrate.

questions.question: Every citizen has a role in protecting Canada's heritage and environment. Which of these does the guide mention?
options: Avoiding waste and pollution while protecting natural, cultural and architectural heritage
questions.explanation: Every citizen has a role to play in avoiding waste and pollution while protecting Canada's natural, cultural and architectural heritage for future generations.

questions.question: True or false: There is compulsory military service in Canada.
questions.explanation: False. There is no compulsory military service in Canada. Serving in the regular forces or the reserves is a voluntary and noble way to contribute.

questions.question: Besides the regular Canadian Forces, which of these does the guide suggest as a way to help protect your community?
options: Serving in the Coast Guard, a police force or a fire department
questions.explanation: You may serve in the Coast Guard or emergency services in your community such as a police force or fire department. Young people can also get involved in the cadets.

questions.question: What is meant by the equality of women and men in Canada?
options: Women and men must hold the same jobs
Men and women are equal under the law
Only men can serve on juries
questions.explanation: In Canada, men and women are equal under the law. Canada's openness does not extend to barbaric cultural practices such as spousal abuse, honour killings, female genital mutilation or forced marriage, which are severely punished under criminal law.
questions.ref: Discover Canada, The Equality of Women and Men (p. 9)

questions.question: Who were the three founding peoples of Canada?
questions.explanation: To understand what it means to be Canadian, it is important to know about our three founding peoples: Aboriginal, French and British.

questions.question: Canada is the only country in North America that is a...
questions.explanation: Canada is the only constitutional monarchy in North America, and we have inherited the oldest continuous constitutional tradition in the world.

questions.question: "Peace, Order and Good Government" is a key phrase from which document?
options: The Charter of Rights and Freedoms (1982)
questions.explanation: Peace, Order and Good Government is a key phrase in Canada's original constitutional document in 1867, the British North America Act.

questions.question: Poets and songwriters have hailed Canada by what nickname?
questions.explanation: Poets and songwriters have hailed Canada as the "Great Dominion," reflecting the prosperous society Canadians built from the Atlantic to the Pacific and the Arctic Circle.

questions.question: John Buchan, Lord Tweedsmuir, was a popular Governor General (1935–40). What did he say immigrant groups should do?
options: Abandon their traditions as quickly as possible
Retain their individuality and each make a contribution to the national character
questions.explanation: Lord Tweedsmuir said immigrant groups "should retain their individuality and each make its contribution to the national character," cherishing both their own traditions and the new loyalty that springs from their union.

questions.question: True or false: Newcomers who have experienced warfare are expected to embrace democratic principles such as the rule of law and must not bring violent or hateful prejudices to Canada.
questions.explanation: True. Experiences of conflict do not justify bringing violent, extreme or hateful prejudices to Canada. In becoming Canadian, newcomers are expected to embrace democratic principles such as the rule of law.

questions.question: True or false: The right to vote comes with a responsibility to vote in federal, provincial or territorial and local elections.
questions.explanation: True. Voting in elections is listed as a citizenship responsibility: the right to vote comes with a responsibility to vote in federal, provincial or territorial and local elections.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in the guide as a citizenship responsibility?
options: Learning to speak both official languages
questions.explanation: The responsibilities listed are obeying the law, taking responsibility for oneself and one's family, serving on a jury, voting in elections, helping others in the community, and protecting heritage and environment. Knowing one official language is required, not both.

questions.question: Canada's institutions uphold a commitment to which three things?
options: Life, Liberty and the Pursuit of Happiness
questions.explanation: Our institutions uphold a commitment to Peace, Order and Good Government, a key phrase in the British North America Act of 1867.

questions.question: True or false: Young people can learn discipline, responsibility and skills by getting involved in the cadets.
questions.explanation: True. The guide says young people can learn discipline, responsibility and skills by getting involved in the cadets.

questions.question: According to the guide, Canada has inherited what from its constitutional past?
options: The oldest continuous constitutional tradition in the world
The newest constitution in the Commonwealth
A constitution written in 1982 from scratch
questions.explanation: Canadians have inherited the oldest continuous constitutional tradition in the world, and Canada is the only constitutional monarchy in North America.
